searchText: What happens when a stateless block is propagated, but the block witness is incomplete? That is, the miner forgot to include a leaf in the witness, but the witness still merkleizes to the correct root, and most transactions can still be processed. <vbuterin> Presumably that block gets ignored and does not get propagated? Yes, the simple (and perhaps best) option is to make it an invalid block. <vbuterin> I guess if a node in the middle happens to be stateful it could just fix the witness <vbuterin> Otherwise yeah, ignore it <alexberegszaszi> If the "canonical witness" idea (= canonical witness hash in the block) is implemented, then such blocks would be just plain invalid and there would be no possibility to "fix" it. Assuming we can satisfy the various prerequisites, the canonical witness approach seems like the best way to address any issues with incomplete or bloated witnesses Yes, bloated witnesses are also interesting. <vbuterin> Question: have we looked at the benefits of hash of witness vs hash of access list? <vbuterin> If you have the access list of the block then you can verify the witness, which is just hashing, and see if it is correct <@273808422753796097> no, but it's probably very good for us to examine the different ways that we want to use witnesses and make sure that whatever hashing scheme we choose is good at supporting those. Merklization/hashing of the access list might work well and be a nice tree structure independent way to do it.
